Two orbits, flown on a fixed rhythm

Every Meridian mission goes to one of two altitude bands. Pick the band your mission needs and we'll match you to the next flight that serves it.

Highlight

Altitudes drawn at twice the scale of Earth's curvature so the bands are readable.

Sun-synchronous orbit
500 to 600 km
Polar, 97 to 98 degrees. Passes over the same spot at the same local time every day, so lighting is consistent for imaging.
Mid-inclination LEO
400 to 480 km
45 or 53 degrees. More passes over populated mid-latitudes and a shorter orbital life, which suits tech demos and student missions.

Payload classes

Prices are per slot and include the dispenser, integration in our cleanroom, one fit check and separation telemetry.

From reservation to separation

The countdown on your payload starts about nine months out. Here's what happens at each mark.

  1. T–9 months

    Reserve a slot

    Tell us the payload class, mass and orbit. We hold a slot on the mission that fits and send the interface control document.

  2. T–6 months

    Interface review

    Our mission engineers check your mass properties, deployables, batteries and deorbit plan against the dispenser and the orbit.

  3. T–10 weeks

    Fit check

    Bring a flight-like unit to Halvard Point. We load it into a dispenser, check clearances and run a separation test.

  4. T–5 weeks

    Final integration

    Your flight unit is loaded and the dispenser closed out in our cleanroom. Battery charging stays available through access ports.

  5. T–0

    Launch and separation

    Each payload deploys on a timed sequence. You get separation confirmation and a first state vector within an hour.

Questions teams ask first

What happens if the launch slips?
Your slot moves with the mission. If the new date no longer works for you, you can move to the next mission with the same orbit at no extra cost, as long as there is room.
Can we fly a payload with propulsion?
Yes. Cold gas, electrospray and other non-pyrotechnic systems are reviewed case by case during the interface review. Propellant must be loaded before you arrive at Halvard Point.
Do you handle export and spectrum paperwork?
We don't file for you, but we tell you exactly which documents we need and when. Most teams start their spectrum filing at the same time they reserve a slot.
How long do payloads stay in orbit?
It depends on altitude, mass and drag area. At 450 km most cubesats decay within four years; at 600 km they can stay more than five. We check every deorbit plan before confirming a slot.

Who flies with us

University teams

Student satellites fly at reduced rates on two slots per mission. Your team gets a named integration engineer, a fit-check rehearsal and a review of your deorbit plan written for first-time teams.

  • Reduced rate on 1U to 6U slots
  • Fit-check rehearsal with your students
  • Paperwork help for spectrum filings

Earth-observation startups

Fly a pathfinder this year and keep a place for the next satellites. Repeat customers can hold slots on up to three future missions, with sun-synchronous options in the morning and afternoon.

  • Hold slots on up to three missions
  • Morning and afternoon SSO
  • Microsat ring for spacecraft up to 60 kg
